clauses.current_legal_basis: The held original text of EO 11689 (37 FR 25987) states no end for this clause. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc: U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09, with laws of 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 not reflected, a stated limit; current-law:ecfr: eCFR as of 2026-10-14; later-events:ofr_catalog: Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) were read with their coverage notes and carry no coverage warning; the U.S. Code search records one hit, the note under 22 U.S.C. 288h that prints this order as an executive document (held at jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t22-s288h.txt, a statute text that authorizes the President to extend these privileges and immunities and still stands, but not a packet source and corroboration only), the eCFR search records one hit and the catalog search no disposition note. The clause therefore continues on the original text, checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: Acting under the Act of October 18, 1972 (Public Law 92-499), the order extends to the Mission to the United States of America of the Commission of the European Communities, to the officers of the Mission assigned to Washington and duly notified to and accepted by the Secretary of State, and to their families, the same privileges and immunities, subject to corresponding conditions and obligations, as are enjoyed by diplomatic missions accredited to the United States and their diplomatic staffs. It has no end date or ending condition of its own and nothing held amends, revokes or supersedes it, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search. EO 11689 (signed 1972-12-05; 37 FR 25987; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11689.txt, read in full) extends diplomatic privileges and immunities to the Mission of the Commission of the European Communities to the United States and to its officers and their families, under Public Law 92-499. Identity: the heading of Executive Order 11689 extending diplomatic privileges and immunities to the Mission of the Commission of the European Communities at 37 FR 25987, the title and the date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory has one clause covering the whole operative text; I confirmed it without correction. Own terms: the order has no end date or ending condition and no savings clause. Later instruments: a search of every held order text for the number 11689 finds only the order's own Federal Register copy and the 1989 codification snapshot. The note to 22 U.S.C. 288h (held current U.S. Code text) prints the order together with EO 12651 of September 9, 1988, which extends privileges to other European Communities offices under the same statute; EO 12651 does not name or revoke EO 11689 in the held text and is not an end. The dossier chain has no event. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record 1, 1 and 0 hits for the order number respectively. Limit stated plainly: the continuing predicate rests on the held original text and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09); 22 U.S.C. 288h, which the order implements, is held and still authorizes the extension, but no held text addresses how the later institutional succession of the European Communities by the European Union bears on the order, and no end is claimed from that.

savings.reason: EO 11689 has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause, and no held instrument ends the extension, so no residual effect is claimed apart from the continuing extension itself.
